lines: A cough won't make it jump.
hero.sub: Sightline Prompter is a teleprompter app for iPhone and Mac. It follows your voice by matching only the words on screen, so a cough, an ad-lib or a skipped line does not throw it. The text stays right under the camera. Free to try.

devices.title: One script.
devices.body: Write on your Mac, record on your iPhone. Both apps share one iCloud script library, so the script is already on your phone when you press record. It is one app on the App Store, and one purchase covers both.
devices.demo_script: Welcome back to the channel. Today I am reading this script straight to the camera. The words keep up with me, so my eyes can stay on the lens.

autosize.title: Sized to
autosize.body: On iPhone, the app estimates how far your face is from the camera, then sets the text size, line length and number of lines to match. Move back and the text grows, lean in and it shrinks. You read comfortably while your eyes stay near the lens.
autosize.mac_note: On Mac, you pick how far you sit, or let the built-in camera measure it. The camera stays off until you turn it on, and nothing is saved or sent.
autosize.script: Look at the lens, take a breath, and say it the way you would say it to a friend.
autosize.cap_note: From here the text stops growing, so each line still fits on the screen.
autosize.caption: Example sizes for an iPhone 16 Pro.

items.title: Record the intro in one take
items.body: Put the script under the front camera and talk to your viewers instead of your notes. The text only moves on the words you actually say, so a breath, a cough or an ad-lib does not cost you your place.
items.alt: Illustrative scene: a creator recording a YouTube intro with Sightline Prompter on iPhone

items.title: Short videos, tight scripts
items.body: Shoot in landscape with a live 9:16 crop guide on screen, so one take works for the horizontal and the vertical cut. The text stays next to the lens in portrait and landscape.
items.alt: Illustrative scene: a person filming a short vertical video on iPhone with the script floating over the preview

items.title: Long lessons, steady pace
items.body: Read a full lesson without scrolling by hand. Add delivery cues in double brackets as reminders. They stay on screen and are never read or counted as words. Words per minute and time left are in Pro.
items.alt: Illustrative scene: an instructor recording an online lesson at a desk with a script on screen

items.title: Under the notch on your Mac
items.body: On a MacBook with a notch, the panel sits right below it, next to the camera, so you look at the people on the call while you read. Macs without a notch get the panel at the top center of the screen.
items.alt: Illustrative scene: a person on a video call on a MacBook with the script panel below the camera notch

crop.title: Stay in
crop.body: Filming landscape for a vertical platform? The iPhone camera shows a live 9:16 crop guide while you shoot, with the rule of thirds and a level line. One landscape take gives you the horizontal video and a vertical cut that keeps your head in frame.

languages.title: Voice following in
languages.body: Voice following works in 31 languages and regional variants, including English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, Mandarin, Cantonese and Turkish. Many are recognized on the device, with no connection.
languages.note: The free version follows your voice in English, Turkish and Spanish, and Sightline Pro adds the rest. Chinese, Japanese and Cantonese are matched in segments, so accuracy is lower than in languages written with spaces.

library.title: Write on Mac.
library.body: Write, search and edit scripts on either device. They sync through iCloud, so nothing needs copying over. Sync uses your iCloud account, and there is no Sightline account. Import what you already have as Word, PDF, Markdown and more.
library.cue_note: Cues in double brackets show on screen as small reminders. They are never read aloud and never counted as words.
library.formats_label: Import: Word, PDF, Markdown, RTF, HTML, OpenDocument, text

items.q: How does a teleprompter that follows your voice work?
items.a: Sightline Prompter listens while you read and matches what it hears to the words on screen. The text moves when you speak and waits when you pause, so you set the pace instead of a scroll speed. It only matches words that are in your script, so a cough, an ad-lib or a skipped line does not make it jump.

items.q: Is there a free teleprompter app that follows your voice?
items.a: Yes. The free version follows your voice for up to 2 minutes per run in English, Turkish and Spanish, and records up to 2 minutes of 1080p video on iPhone. Sightline Pro removes the limits.

Many languages are recognized on the device, so they work without a connection. If a language has no offline model installed, the audio goes to Apple's speech service, and the app says so on screen. Turkish needs the iOS Dictation model for on-device recognition.

31 languages and regional variants, including English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, Mandarin, Cantonese and Turkish. The free version covers English, Turkish and Spanish. Chinese, Japanese and Cantonese are matched in segments, so accuracy is lower than in languages written with spaces.

items.q: What if I go off script?
items.a: It stays where you are. A cough, an ad-lib or a skipped line does not make the text jump. It only moves when you say words that are on screen.

items.q: Do I need a MacBook with a notch?
items.a: No. On a MacBook with a notch, the panel sits right below it. On a Mac without one, the panel sits at the top center of the screen.

items.q: How does auto text size work?
items.a: On iPhone, the front camera estimates how far your face is from the screen and sizes the text so the letters keep the same visual angle, which keeps them comfortable to read at that distance. It also limits line length and the number of lines, so your eyes stay near the lens. On Mac, you choose a distance preset or turn on the optional camera measurement. Everything is measured on your device, and no video or face data leaves it.

Yes, on iPhone. The app records with the script floating over the live preview and saves the video to your Photos library. The Mac app is a prompter panel for calls and recordings you make with other tools.

items.q: Does one purchase cover iPhone and Mac?
items.a: Yes. It is one app on the App Store, and Sightline Pro unlocks both the iPhone and the Mac version. Both use the same iCloud script library.
Sightline Pro is available as a subscription (with a free trial) or as a one-time purchase. The App Store shows current prices in your local currency.
Plain text, Markdown, Word, PDF, RTF, HTML and OpenDocument files. Scripts sync between iPhone and Mac through iCloud.

items.q: Can I use a game controller?
items.a: Yes. A DualSense controller works with the Mac app over Bluetooth or USB: the analog stick scrolls, and buttons change speed and jump between paragraphs. Controller support is part of Sightline Pro.

Your scripts stay in your own iCloud Drive. There are no ads, no Sightline account and no tracking across apps. Sync uses your iCloud account, so you need to be signed in to iCloud on the device. Anonymous usage counts can be switched off in Settings.
